reasoning: This is a narrative review article discussing clinical presentation, aetiology, pathophysiology, and treatment of cognitive deficits in schizophrenia. It synthesizes existing literature without generating or using new research software or research data itself (no new datasets, code, or tools are produced or applied). This is a consensus guideline paper synthesizing existing literature and expert opinion to produce clinical recommendations. It does not generate or use any research software, nor does it create or analyze new research data (no dataset, corpus, or empirical data collection). It is a narrative/expert review resulting in clinical guidance, fitting the 'Other' category for both software and data.

The study uses existing research software (TopoToolbox V2) to process a national DEM, but does not create or extend software itself—this counts as software used, generating new knowledge via analysis. The core contribution is a newly created national-scale geodatabase of catchment and stream morphometric characteristics for the Philippines, derived from the DEM and organized into a novel dataset (with an interactive web-app for access). This constitutes generation of substantive new research data, placing it in D1. Hence S2D1.

The authors developed a new visualization tool/software that applies the Jaya algorithm (with Latin Hypercube Sampling enhancement) to graph drawing, representing newly created research software used to generate novel layout results. They also generated synthetic graph datasets using the Erdős–Rényi model (and used real-world graphs) specifically for benchmarking their method, constituting newly created research data substantively used to produce new findings. Hence both software and data were generated as part of the research.

This is a study protocol for a planned randomised clinical trial. No research has been conducted yet, no software was generated or used to produce findings, and no data has been collected or analysed at this stage. Per the general rules, planned or proposed artefacts (future data collection, outcome assessments) do not count as evidence of actual data use/generation. Hence it falls under S3D3.

This study generated new survey/interview data (literature review, interviews, surveys of 153 nurses across four cohorts) to assess competencies and confidence in genomics, creating new primary research data analysed via thematic and statistical methods. No research software was developed or substantively used beyond standard statistical/survey tools, so it falls under S3. Since new data was collected specifically for this research, it is classified as D1.

The study uses patient DW-MRI data from ten GBM patients to derive cellular density maps and TCP maps, generating new research data (ADC-derived cellularity/TCP maps, dose escalation plans) specific to this in-silico study. This constitutes generated substantive data. While the research involves computational modeling (TCP models, treatment planning software), there is no indication that new research software was developed or significantly extended; existing planning/modeling tools and mathematical models were applied as utilities rather than as a novel software contribution, so this falls under 'No Research Software' (S3).

This is a histopathology/immunology study applying multiplexed immunofluorescence to patient lymph node tissue samples to generate new quantitative data on immune cell phenotypes across NLPHL and THRLBCL cases. The research data (immune cell phenotype quantifications, spatial patterns) are newly generated through the research, so D1 applies. The study likely used existing imaging/analysis software (e.g. image analysis platforms for multiplexed IF, cell phenotyping software) as a tool/utility rather than developing new software - no indication of novel software creation, so S2 (existing software used to generate new data/knowledge).

The study collected new survey data (384 startup directors/representatives, using BRCS, MBI-GS, and custom Covid-19 stress assessments) specifically for this research, which constitutes newly generated research data (D1). For analysis, the researchers used the GMDH neural network methodology - an existing modeling approach/algorithm - to analyze the data and select effective parameters, rather than developing new software/tooling; this is a research method applied to generate new knowledge from the data, treated as software used (S2) since GMDH is an established neural network approach used as an analytic tool rather than software created/extended by the authors.

The study generates new experimental research data: a novel crystal structure of AMG-176 bound to Mcl-1, along with NMR conformer analysis data for the clinical inhibitors. This constitutes substantive data generation central to the findings (new knowledge about induced fit and ligand rigidity). The paper does not describe development or significant extension of any research software; standard crystallography/NMR analysis tools would be used only as routine utilities, not as a contribution of the research itself. Hence it falls into No Software, Data Generated.

This is a cluster RCT that collected new primary data (maternal and child health outcomes, CHW performance measures) across 8 clinics over 2 years, generating a novel dataset for the study. There is no mention of developing or substantively using specialized research software; standard statistical analysis tools would be utility software, not research software generating new knowledge. Hence data generated (D1), no research software (S3).

The study analyzed existing EHR data from UK Biobank and CPRD Gold linked to cancer registry data, but developed new research data in the form of harmonised symptom/test phenotypes (coded algorithms applied to EHR data creating new derived datasets of symptom recording rates) that generate new knowledge about cancer presentation differences. This constitutes substantive data generation (new phenotype datasets/classifications). No research software (new code/tools) is described as being created or used beyond standard statistical modelling (Poisson regression), which is a routine utility rather than a research software contribution.

This is a perspective/opinion piece discussing decolonisation of the psychology curriculum. It does not report the creation or use of any research software, nor does it generate or use any research data (e.g., datasets, corpora, empirical results). It is purely a conceptual/argumentative discussion with recommendations, so it falls under S3 (no research software) and D3 (no research data).

The paper's main contribution is the compilation of a new global dataset (DOCU-CLIM) of 621 documentary climate time series, including previously unpublished data, which constitutes research data generation. The paper focuses on data compilation and validation (using proxy forward models) rather than developing or significantly extending any research software; any computational tools used (e.g., for correlation analysis) appear to be standard utilities rather than novel research software central to generating new knowledge.

The study developed a novel explainable multimodal network model/AI framework specifically for linking biodiversity to environmental change (research software generated and used to produce new knowledge), and it generated new substantive research data through sediment core multilocus metabarcoding, biocide measurements, and paleolimnological records spanning 100 years - these are newly generated datasets, not just reuse of existing public data. Both the custom AI/network modeling approach and the 100-year biodiversity/environmental dataset derived from the lake sediment core were created as part of this research to generate new knowledge about ecosystem shifts.

This is a narrative/state-of-the-art review article summarizing existing literature on blood-brain barrier imaging techniques and clinical applications. It does not report generation or use of any specific research software, nor does it generate or analyze a specific research dataset. It is a synthesis of prior studies and discussion of methodologies at a conceptual level, fitting the "no software, no data" category.

This is a cross-sectional survey study in which the researchers collected new primary survey data from 10,007 respondents in Malang, Indonesia, specifically for this research (knowledge, willingness, vaccine uptake questionnaire). This constitutes generated research data. The statistical analyses (linear regression, logistic regression, GSEM) were performed using standard statistical software (e.g., Stata/SPSS) as a utility tool, not a novel research software contribution, so no research software was generated.

This is a review article discussing concepts, challenges, and published GWAS/post-GWAS findings related to Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease microglial genetics. It does not report generation or use of any specific new software tool, nor does it generate or analyze a novel dataset itself; it synthesizes existing literature and discusses computational tools/datasets conceptually without performing new analyses. Hence no research software or data artifacts are produced or substantively used within this paper.

This is a review article summarizing existing literature on MAIT cells and the microbiome. It does not report generation or use of any specific research software, nor does it generate or analyze new research data/datasets. It is purely a narrative synthesis of prior findings, with no computational tools or empirical datasets described.

The authors developed a novel counterfactual GAN architecture specifically for this research, which generates new synthetic OCT images and enables new analyses—this constitutes generated research software (S1), as new knowledge (retinal aging insights) is created through this custom software. The underlying OCT imaging data, however, is from the existing UK Biobank population study, an external dataset used but not created by this research, classifying it as D2 (data used).

The researchers used an existing pre-trained model (GPT-2) as research software to generate simulated narratives by manipulating stochasticity and memory span parameters. This process generated new data (the simulated FTD-like narratives and NLP measure outputs) that were analyzed to produce new scientific knowledge about NLP markers of thought disorder. While they provide a Python tutorial, this is a utility/dissemination tool rather than a novel research software contribution - GPT-2 itself was used, not created. However, the simulated narrative datasets constitute newly generated research data central to the findings.

This is a study protocol describing a planned cross-sectional survey. No software was developed (Qualtrics is used as a routine utility tool, not research software), and no data has yet been collected or analyzed - the survey is planned for future dissemination and analysis. Since this is a protocol for future work rather than reporting completed research with actual data/software generation or use, it falls under S3D3 per the general rule that planned/proposed artefacts are not considered as evidence of use or generation.

This paper reports two phase 1 clinical drug-drug interaction trials in healthy subjects, generating new pharmacokinetic data (Cmax, AUC values) for rezafungin coadministered with various drugs. This is clearly newly generated clinical/research data. There is no indication of any research software being created or used in a substantive way to generate new knowledge—standard statistical/PK analysis tools would be routine utilities, not the focus of the paper. Hence classified as No Software, Data Generated."

The paper derives new adherence scores (total and partial 5-point scores) for large subsets of UK Biobank participants by applying a standardized scoring methodology to existing UK Biobank data (anthropometric, dietary, physical activity). This constitutes generation of new research data (the derived scores/variables) that create new knowledge about adherence to cancer prevention recommendations, even though it uses existing UK Biobank raw data. No new research software is described - they used standard statistical/epidemiological methods and existing cohort data infrastructure rather than developing new software tools.

This is a narrative literature review discussing existing cardiovascular risk prediction methods, biomarkers, and ocular imaging approaches. It does not report generation or use of any specific research software, nor does it generate or analyze a specific dataset. It synthesizes prior literature without producing new data or software artifacts.

The study uses Google Trends (existing software tool/data platform) to download search volume data, which is existing data (not generated by the researchers). They also use Joinpoint regression software (an existing statistical tool) to analyze the data. No new research software was created, and no new research data was generated—only existing Google Trends data was used to produce new findings/knowledge about search behavior patterns during the mpox outbreak.

This qualitative study collected new primary data via semi-structured in-depth interviews with 30 Dental Officers and 17 Dental Managers in Fiji, which was then thematically analyzed to derive novel themes about COVID-19's effect on dental services. This constitutes generation of new research data (interview data/transcripts). No research software was created or used substantively; manual thematic analysis was conducted, implying no specialized software tool was integral to generating new knowledge.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis that synthesizes data extracted from 76 articles and 2 national surveys to compute pooled prevalence estimates (stunting, thinness, overweight/obesity, micronutrient deficiencies). The meta-analysis generates new aggregated data/knowledge (pooled estimates) through synthesis of existing study results, which constitutes substantive data generation (D1). No research software was developed or used in a substantive, knowledge-generating way beyond standard statistical tools for meta-analysis, so it falls under S3 (no research software).

The study generated new experimental data (HD-sEMG recordings decomposed into motor unit firing characteristics) from 18 children, which constitutes newly created research data generating new knowledge about DCD vs TD children's motor unit behavior. For software, they used existing decomposition algorithms/software (e.g., EMG decomposition tools) to process the signals, but did not report developing or significantly extending new software - it was used as a tool to derive results, fitting the 'used' category rather than 'generated'.
